outcome: Abnormal credential use is challenged or blocked as it happens, and stale, over-privileged directory accounts are closed down instead of forgotten.
overview: Once an attacker holds one set of credentials in a manufacturing estate, the directory is usually what carries them everywhere else: service accounts with old passwords, administrators who never log off, and trust relationships nobody has reviewed since a merger. Falcon Identity Protection watches authentication behaviour rather than endpoints, so a credential being used abnormally becomes visible. The first output is almost always a directory hygiene report, and acting on it usually reduces exposure more than the detection capability does.

benefits.text: Abnormal use of a valid credential is detected rather than treated as legitimate access
benefits.limits: Behavioural baselining needs a learning period; detections before it completes are noisier and should not set expectations

benefits.text: Directory hygiene problems — stale accounts, privilege sprawl, weak service accounts — become visible
benefits.limits: Visibility is not remediation, and the remediation is organisational work the platform cannot perform

benefits.text: Risky authentications can be challenged or blocked rather than only alerted on
benefits.limits: The platform is agent-and-cloud, so telemetry leaves the customer estate; the tenant region is a design decision to be made and recorded rather than a default to be accepted

residency: Authentication telemetry is processed in the vendor cloud in a selected tenant region, recorded at design

notFor.situation: An estate whose identity is entirely cloud-native with strong conditional access already enforced
notFor.why: The directory attack paths this addresses are largely closed in that architecture

notFor.situation: An organisation unwilling to act on directory hygiene findings
notFor.why: The findings are where most of the exposure reduction comes from; detection alone leaves it in place

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited CrowdStrike implementation partner · Duration: 6–10 weeks including a learning period that is not compressible
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed hygiene review.
1) Deploy — directory sensors installed, observation started
2) Learn — behavioural baseline established, service-account dependencies mapped
3) Report — hygiene findings produced with owners and dates
4) Enforce and hand over — enforcement enabled per account class, findings review handed over
deliverables: A test of abnormal credential use is detected and, where enforcement applies, challenged
Every hygiene finding carries an owner and a date
Service-account enforcement is enabled only with recorded dependency sign-off
